title: Blocking TransferEngine on the caller's thread, without Vert.x (ADR-0012 option A)
requirement: Plan §20 RT-03 (slice RT-03c); ADR-0012 decisions 2 and 6; concurrency conventions §1 and §2; register OBS-07
acceptance: transfer(TransferRequest) runs on the calling thread and needs no Vert.x instance
A transfer beyond maxConcurrentTransfers is rejected with TransferException; a freed slot is reused
A failed attempt is retried up to maxRetryAttempts; exhausting retries returns FAILED
cancelTransfer(jobId) ends that transfer promptly as CANCELLED, without a retry, with the message "Transfer cancelled", and without leaving the caller's thread interrupted
Cancelling one transfer does not affect another transfer of the same protocol
shutdown(Duration) cancels running transfers, returns once they have ended, and rejects new transfers
An interrupt the engine did not send ends the transfer as CANCELLED without a retry and stays set
classification: external-path behavioral (every transfer goes through a real local HTTP server)

preparatoryRefactor.result: 104 tests, 0 failures (the new test class was held out of this run)
preparatoryRefactor.change: ProtocolFactory gained constructors without Vert.x; the Vert.x constructors are deprecated and ignore the instance, which no adapter has needed since RT-03b. Behaviour-preserving.

discardedAttempts.name: red attempt 1
discardedAttempts.reason: Test defect: five tests waited on the server handshake with an unbounded join. The red-stage stub throws before any request, so each hung until the 30-second preemptive timeout. The wait now completes when either the server signals or the transfer ends.

discardedAttempts.name: affected-modules attempt 1
discardedAttempts.reason: TransferExecutionServiceTest.testDeprecatedConstructorClosesOwnedVertx timed out. The shutdown chain was composed on a future bound to the service's own Vert.x context, so its continuation was never dispatched once that instance closed.

discardedAttempts.name: agent attempt 1
discardedAttempts.reason: First fix moved only the close to a virtual thread; the continuation was still bound to the closed context. Fixed by running the whole owned-instance shutdown on one virtual thread and completing a promise bound to no context.

discardedAttempts.name: first full regression
discardedAttempts.reason: Stopped deliberately after a reporting gap was found (below); its processes were verified by command line and parent chain before being stopped. No log retained.

red.result: 8 tests, 8 errors, each on the RT-03c stub (UnsupportedOperationException), within 9 seconds
red.revision: 6a2864c plus the preparatory refactor, the stub constructor and methods, and the tests

green.change: SimpleTransferEngine rewritten: blocking transfer on the caller's thread, a semaphore for the limit, retries with interruptible back-off, per-transfer cancellation by interrupt guarded against the completion race, and shutdown(Duration). TransferEngine has no Vert.x types.

secondCycle.reason: Found during regression: the agent reports the message of any unsuccessful result, and a cancelled job carried none, so a transfer cancelled at agent shutdown would have been reported as "Unknown error".

red.result: 8 tests, 1 failure: the cancelled result had no error message

mutants.name: m1-no-interrupt
mutants.result: detected by three cancellation and shutdown tests

mutants.name: m5-interrupt-ignored
mutants.result: survived the first run: with retries allowed, the interruptible back-off also ends the transfer as CANCELLED. The outside-interrupt test was changed to use no retries, and the mutant is then detected. The first, surviving run's log was overwritten by the rerun.

refactor: OBS-07: DEBUG statements in SimpleTransferEngine reduced from 37 to 3. Callers moved: the agent and workflow call the blocking engine through their own vertx.executeBlocking until RT-05 and RT-04; the examples fork concurrent transfers in a TaskScope and bound them with its deadline. Tests moved: SimpleTransferEngineTest, SimpleTransferEngineBidirectionalTest, BasicTransferIntegrationTest (its 10 ms polling loop replaced by a deterministic check in the blocking test), SftpAbortIntegrationTest, the workflow TestTransferEngine, and the examples IntegrationTestSuite.
behaviourChanges: A cancelled transfer ends as CANCELLED with the message "Transfer cancelled"; it previously ended as FAILED
Cancelling a transfer no longer calls the shared adapter abort(), which affected other transfers (ENG-09)
A second transfer with the ID of a running one is rejected instead of silently replacing its tracking
The engine no longer clears the caller's MDC when a transfer ends
The examples passed 1,048,576 as the retry delay in milliseconds (about 17 minutes), believing it was a chunk size; they now pass 1,000

characterization.classification: retrospective characterization: written after the code, once coverage showed the duplicate-ID rejection (new in this slice) and the pause path had no test. Test-only; the regression below ran on the same production code.

coverageAfterRegression.SimpleTransferEngine: lines 202/240, branches 63/90 (before the two characterization tests)

regression.result: per-module totals (core, workflow, tenant, controller, agent): 1582 run, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped; 134 run, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped; 64 run, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped; 574 run, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped; 101 run, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped

limitations: On a platform thread, such as the Vert.x worker the agent still uses, an interrupt does not close a blocked socket, so cancellation waits for the adapter's next interrupt check or socket timeout. The agent does not cancel transfers today; RT-05 moves it to virtual threads.
shutdown(Duration) returning false (a transfer that ignores cancellation) is not exercised by a test.
CI has never passed (ENG-07, deferred by SEQ-01); the regression evidence is the local run above.
sensitiveDataCheck: Logs contain Maven and test output only; no request bodies, credentials, keys or sensitive payloads.
